## https://udyoggrowth.com/school-affiliation-consultant/
School Affiliation Consultant — CBSE, CISCE | Udyog Growth Udyog Growth ☰ Subsidies GST GeM & Tenders MSME Import-Export Environment NGO/CSR Loans Call Home / School Affiliation & Recognition Consultancy School Affiliation & Recognition Consultant — CBSE, CISCE, DoE Recognition (New Delhi) Quick answer: 2025-26 rule change most consultants haven't caught up with: CBSE's State NOC is now optional — apply with or without it, and if the state stays silent for 30 days (plus a 15-day reminder), a deemed-NOC applies. But the State Recognition Certificate is still mandatory — no NOC does not mean no state clearance. Land area now only sets your school's category ; built-up area decides how many sections you can run (3 per 400 sq m). Filed via CBSE's SARAS 7.0 portal. The Rs 5 lakh "security deposit" myth: widely repeated online, but there is no such mandatory deposit for a senior secondary school. The Rs 5,00,000 figure in CBSE's fee schedule is the society-to-society transfer fee — a completely different head. Official fresh-affiliation fees are far lower: Rs 1,50,000 up to Secondary, Rs 2,50,000 up to Senior Secondary, plus Rs 5,000 annual. We work from the current fee schedule, not recycled blog numbers. CBSE affiliation — eligibility, land, fees Only a registered Society, Public Trust or Section 8 company can hold CBSE affiliation — never a proprietary or for-profit company. Affiliation is staged: fresh affiliation up to Secondary first (initial term 3 years), Senior Secondary comes by upgradation after running Classes 9-10, then 5-year extension cycles. Land category Where Minimum land Category C Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad + NE/island states 1,600–2,400 sq m Category B Y-category cities, state capitals, hilly areas 2,400–3,200 sq m Category A Anywhere else 6,000 sq m Land only sets your category now — sections are decided by built-up area (3 sections per 400 sq m, certified by the local body or a licensed architect). This decoupling, clarified via CBSE Notification No. 06/2026, changes how much you can actually run on a given plot — a distinction most consultants still get wrong. Fee head Amount Fresh affiliation up to Senior Secondary ₹2,50,000 Fresh affiliation up to Secondary ₹1,50,000 Middle Class Syllabus (Classes 1–5) ₹50,000 Annual fee ₹5,000 Re-inspection / periodical inspection ₹50,000 each Society-to-society transfer ₹5,00,000 SARAS 7.0 — the current application cycle CBSE now runs affiliation through the SARAS portal (currently version 7.0) . Two pre-conditions before you can even file: a UDISE+ code and a completed SQAAF self-assessment . Fresh affiliation and upgradation applications now attract a mandatory 100% physical inspection — there is no longer a documents-only fast track. We track every SARAS window and portal update so a client's file is ready the day it opens, not scrambling after a deadline extension. CISCE / ICSE affiliation The Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations affiliates schools to a similarly non-profit entity (Society/Trust/Section 8 company), with comparable land, staffing and PTR expectations, a qualified principal (5+ years' experience), and a properly constituted managing committee. CISCE affiliation hinges heavily on the inspection report — we prepare the file and the premises together, not sequentially. Delhi Directorate of Education recognition The DoE has scrapped the old "essentiality certificate" requirement and moved to a self-certification model — a school certifies against a checklist of infrastructure, safety, teacher and PTR standards (73 checkpoints, down from 91) rather than waiting on a discretionary essentiality clearance. Recognition under the Delhi School Education Act & Rules, 1973 remains mandatory regardless of CBSE's own optional-NOC change — the two are separate documents, and a school still needs the State Recognition Certificate before its CBSE/CISCE file can go through. Since November 2025 , the DoE has also moved to recognise private unaided schools operating in previously non-conforming areas — bringing an estimated ~500 additional schools under DoE oversight and creating roughly 20,000 extra EWS/DG/CWSN seats citywide. If your school (or a site you're evaluating) sits in an area that was earlier treated as non-conforming, this is worth re-checking before assuming recognition is blocked. RTE compliance & the 25% EWS quota Private unaided non-minority schools must reserve 25% of entry-level seats for EWS/DG students under Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act, with state fee reimbursement under Section 12(2). Delhi runs a computerised EWS lottery (the 2025-26 draw allotted around 42,000 seats). A Supreme Court bench, by order dated 13 January 2026, directed that securing this quota be treated as a national mission and impleaded the NCPCR to monitor compliance — enforcement is tightening, not easing. We help schools build the compliant admission and reimbursement-claim process from the outset rather than fixing it under audit pressure. UDISE+ registration The 11-digit UDISE+ code is filed via Form A02 through your Block/District MIS office — not a self-serve online form — and requires state recognition first. Realistic timelines run 4-6 weeks in metros to 8-12 weeks in rural areas; the July-September window gets congested. Since UDISE+ is itself a SARAS pre-condition, a delay here delays affiliation. Fire & building safety NOC for schools An educational building in Delhi taller than 9 m or with ground plus 2 upper storeys needs a fire safety certificate under the Delhi Fire Service Act 2007 and NBC 2016 Part 4 — a two-stage process (pre-construction plan approval, then post-construction certification), typically valid 3 years, filed through the Delhi Fire Service. A separate building-safety/structural-stability certificate from the local body or a licensed architect is required for CBSE regardless of the fire NOC. School canteen FSSAI, entity formation & educational land Three approvals in this journey are already deep specialities of ours on other pages — we run them as one file for a school client rather than three separate engagements: FSSAI registration/license for the canteen or hostel mess (HFSS-food restrictions apply within and near school premises), Society/Trust/Section 8 company formation for the school's managing body, and change of land use (CLU) for educational purposes in Delhi if the site isn't already zoned for institutional use. School bus & transport compliance CBSE-mandated norms (implementing Supreme Court guidelines under the Motor Vehicles Act 1988): yellow paint with "School Bus"/"On School Duty" signage, a speed governor capped at 40 km/h, GPS and CCTV, grilled windows with mesh, a female attendant, a trained driver with a clean record, a designated Transport Manager, and a valid RTO permit from the state transport department. Who this is for Trusts and societies setting up a new CBSE, CISCE or DoE-recognised school anywhere in Delhi; existing schools whose affiliation is up for extension or Senior Secondary upgradation; schools whose SARAS application stalled at inspection; and managing bodies untangling land-category, NOC or EWS-compliance confusion under the 2025-26 rule changes. Setting up a school, or stuck on SARAS, NOC or recognition? Call for a free consultation Our methodology: precision, persistence, presence Procedural mastery — we prepare every file to meet the specific technical criteria of the relevant department, minimising queries and delays. Dedicated liaison — consistent follow-up on your application so it keeps moving through the standard workflow. Compliance-first documentation — built to withstand scrutiny, protecting your business from future audits or objections. Frequently Asked Questions Is CBSE State NOC still mandatory for a new school in 2026? No — from the 2026-27 session, CBSE's State NOC is optional. A school can apply with or without it; if without, CBSE refers the matter to the state, and a deemed-NOC applies if the state stays silent for 30 days plus a 15-day reminder. This does not remove the separate, still-mandatory State Recognition Certificate under the RTE Act — the two are different documents. How much land do I need to open a CBSE school? It depends on land category: 1,600-2,400 sq m in Category C cities (Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and a few other areas), 2,400-3,200 sq m in Category B, and 6,000 sq m in Category A elsewhere. Note land area now only sets your category — the number of sections you can actually run is governed separately by built-up area, at 3 sections per 400 sq m. How much does CBSE affiliation actually cost? Official fees: Rs 1,50,000 for fresh affiliation up to Secondary, Rs 2,50,000 up to Senior Secondary, Rs 50,000 for the Middle Class Syllabus (Classes 1-5), and Rs 5,000 annual. There is no mandatory Rs 5 lakh 'security deposit' for a senior secondary school — that figure is the separate society-to-society transfer fee, often misquoted online. Can a private company set up and run a CBSE school? No — CBSE only affiliates schools run by a registered Society, Public Trust or Section 8 (not-for-profit) company. A proprietary or for-profit private limited company cannot hold CBSE affiliation, so the first step for a new school is choosing and registering the right non-profit entity. What is SARAS 7.0 and what do I need before applying? SARAS is CBSE's online affiliation portal, currently on version 7.0. Two pre-conditions before filing: a UDISE+ code and a completed SQAAF self-assessment. Fresh affiliation and upgradation applications now require a mandatory 100% physical inspection — there's no documents-only route anymore. Do I need a UDISE+ code before applying for CBSE affiliation? Yes — UDISE+ is a precondition for filing on SARAS. It's an 11-digit code obtained via Form A02 through your Block/District MIS office (not a self-serve online form), and it requires state recognition to already be in place. Budget 4-6 weeks in metros to 8-12 weeks in rural areas, and avoid applying in the congested July-September window. What fire safety rules apply to a school building in Delhi? A school building taller than 9 m, or with ground plus 2 upper storeys, needs a Delhi Fire Service certificate under the Delhi Fire Service Act 2007 and NBC 2016 — a two-stage process covering pre-construction plan approval and post-construction certification, typically valid 3 years. This is separate from, and in addition to, the building-safety/structural-stability certificate CBSE requires. Is the 25% EWS quota compulsory for private schools, and is enforcement getting stricter? Yes — Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act requires private unaided non-minority schools to reserve 25% of entry-level seats for EWS/DG students, with state fee reimbursement. A Supreme Court bench, by order dated 13 January 2026, directed that this be treated as a national mission and brought in the NCPCR to monitor compliance — schools should expect tighter enforcement, not a rollback. My school's land was earlier in a "non-conforming area" — can it still be recognised? Possibly, and more easily than before. Since November 2025 the DoE has moved to recognise private unaided schools even in previously non-conforming areas, bringing an estimated 500 additional schools under its oversight. Zoning and land-use still need to be checked and, if required, regularised — but the blanket bar that existed earlier has been relaxed. Do I need a separate FSSAI license for the school canteen? Yes — canteens and hostel mess facilities need FSSAI Basic Registration or a State License depending on turnover, and FSSAI's charter separately restricts high-fat/sugar/salt (HFSS) food within and near school premises. We run this alongside the affiliation file rather than as an afterthought — see our dedicated FSSAI page for the full slab and process detail. What happens if my CBSE affiliation extension lapses? A lapsed extension puts the school's ability to conduct board exams and issue valid certificates at risk. Extension fees are tiered by how late you apply (Rs 50,000-1,50,000) plus a late fee of Rs 25,000/month capped at Rs 1,00,000 — so the cost of delay compounds quickly. We track extension timelines for clients well before the 5-year cycle turns over. © 2026 Udyog Growth. Puram's network are required to break the tie via a draw of lots conducted in front of parents and recorded on video, per Delhi DoE rules. Where do DPS R.K. Puram's youngest students study? ## https://udyoggrowth.com/solar-subsidy-pm-surya-ghar/
PM Surya Ghar Solar Subsidy — ₹78,000 Claim | Udyog Growth Udyog Growth ☰ Subsidies GST GeM & Tenders MSME Import-Export Environment NGO/CSR Loans Call Home / Solar Subsidy (PM Surya Ghar) PM Surya Ghar Solar Subsidy — Claim, Net Metering & Rejection-Proofing (Delhi-NCR) Quick answer: Residential subsidy under PM Surya Ghar: ₹30,000 per kW up to 2 kW , plus ₹18,000 for the 3rd kW — capped at ₹78,000 for 3 kW and above (₹30,000 for 1 kW, ₹60,000 for 2 kW). Paid by DBT, typically 30–45 days after DISCOM commissioning. Apply on pmsuryaghar.gov.in; equipment must be ALMM-listed ; group housing societies get ₹18,000/kW for common facilities up to 500 kW. The #1 reason subsidy claims get rejected: a panel or inverter that isn't on the MNRE ALMM list — followed by the electricity-connection name not matching the applicant. Both are checked after you've spent the money, so we verify vendor, equipment and paperwork before installation, not at claim stage. What you actually get System size Subsidy 1 kW ₹30,000 2 kW ₹60,000 3 kW and above ₹78,000 (cap) Group housing society / RWA (common facilities) ₹18,000 per kW, up to 500 kW (max 3 kW per house) Eligibility: a residential electricity connection with sanctioned load up to 10 kW, the application in the same name as the electricity bill, and no earlier rooftop-solar subsidy on the connection. The claim sequence — where files get stuck Portal registration on pmsuryaghar.gov.in with DISCOM and consumer number. Feasibility approval from the DISCOM — sanctioned-load and technical checks happen here. Installation by a registered vendor with ALMM-listed panels and inverter — the step where a wrong equipment choice silently kills the subsidy. Net metering + commissioning — meter installation and DISCOM inspection. DBT disbursal — bank details on the portal; money typically lands 30–45 days after commissioning. We chase every stage so the file never idles. Commercial & industrial rooftops — a different game PM Surya Ghar is residential; shops, offices and factories don't get this subsidy. Commercial rooftop works on economics instead: net-metering/net-billing arrangements with your DISCOM, capex-vs-PPA structuring (third-party investor owns the plant, you buy power cheaper), and the accounting treatment of the asset. We structure the DISCOM approvals and the PPA so the project stands on savings, not on a subsidy that doesn't exist for you. Factory or commercial installation as part of a bigger setup? Solar sits alongside pollution consents and the project-finance file — we handle the full approval stack. Who this is for Homeowners across Delhi, Noida, Greater Noida, Ghaziabad, Gurugram and Faridabad claiming the subsidy correctly the first time; RWAs and group housing societies for common-area systems; applicants whose claim is stuck or was rejected; and businesses evaluating commercial rooftop with net metering or a PPA. Want the subsidy without the rejection cycle? Call for a free consultation Our methodology: precision, persistence, presence Procedural mastery — we prepare every file to meet the specific technical criteria of the relevant department, minimising queries and delays. Dedicated liaison — consistent follow-up on your application so it keeps moving through the standard workflow. Compliance-first documentation — built to withstand scrutiny, protecting your business from future audits or objections. Frequently Asked Questions How much subsidy do I get under PM Surya Ghar? Rs 30,000 per kW for the first 2 kW, plus Rs 18,000 for the 3rd kW — capped at Rs 78,000 for systems of 3 kW or more. So 1 kW gets Rs 30,000, 2 kW gets Rs 60,000, and 3 kW or larger gets Rs 78,000, paid by DBT to your bank account after DISCOM commissioning. Who is eligible for the PM Surya Ghar subsidy? A residential consumer with sanctioned load up to 10 kW, applying in the same name as on the electricity bill, with no earlier rooftop-solar subsidy on that connection. Group housing societies and RWAs are separately eligible at Rs 18,000/kW for common facilities up to 500 kW (max 3 kW per house). Why do PM Surya Ghar subsidy claims get rejected? The most common cause is equipment — a panel or inverter not on the MNRE ALMM list — followed by the applicant's name not matching the electricity connection, and missing roof-ownership proof. All three are preventable before installation; almost none are fixable after. We verify the vendor's equipment list against ALMM before you sign. How long does the subsidy take to arrive? Typically 30–45 days after the DISCOM commissions the plant and your bank details are verified on the portal. Delays usually trace to pending DISCOM inspection or a bank-detail mismatch — both chase-able, which is exactly what we do. Can my shop, office or factory get the PM Surya Ghar subsidy? No — the scheme is for residential connections. Commercial and industrial rooftops work on net-metering/net-billing economics and PPA structuring instead, which often beats a subsidy anyway at commercial tariffs. We structure the DISCOM approvals and the PPA for exactly this. Is there a loan available for rooftop solar under the scheme? Banks run dedicated PM Surya Ghar loan products for residential systems with simplified processing. Whether a loan makes sense depends on your tariff and consumption; we run the payback math with and without financing before you commit. © 2026 Udyog Growth.
